speaker: Me
text: Okay, let's get started. Today we need to settle the Q1 roadmap for the analytics product. I want us to leave with a ranked list.

speaker: Speaker 1
text: I put together a draft last week. Four candidates: self-serve dashboards, the scheduled report exports, the Snowflake connector and SSO.

speaker: Me
text: Right. Which of those do customers ask for most? Lena, you looked at the support tickets.

speaker: Speaker 3
text: Yes. Out of about two hundred tickets in October, forty-one mention exports, thirty-three ask for the Snowflake connector, and SSO comes up mostly with the larger accounts.

speaker: Speaker 2
text: From the design side, self-serve dashboards would be the biggest change. We'd need a whole new editor, I'd say eight to ten weeks.

speaker: Me
text: That would eat most of the quarter. Priya, what's the engineering estimate for the exports?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: Scheduled exports are about three weeks. We already have the query layer, so it's mostly the scheduler and the email delivery. CSV and PDF first, Excel later.

speaker: Speaker 1
text: The Snowflake connector is more uncertain. Four to six weeks, depending on how we handle credentials.

speaker: Me
text: So exports plus the connector fits into Q1 if we postpone the dashboards. What does that do to the Contoso conversation?

speaker: Speaker 3
text: Contoso Retail told us twice they want weekly exports for their store managers. The connector matters to two other prospects in the pipeline.

speaker: Speaker 2
text: I'm a bit worried that we keep pushing dashboards. Sales keeps demoing the old editor and people find it clunky.

speaker: Me
text: Fair. What if you do a design spike in January, no engineering, just prototypes, so we can start the build in Q2 with confidence?

speaker: Speaker 2
text: That works. I'd want two customer sessions to validate it.

speaker: Speaker 1
text: One more topic: SSO. If we skip it, we might lose the two enterprise deals. Can we at least do SAML only, not the whole identity provider zoo?

speaker: Me
text: How long would SAML only take?

speaker: Speaker 1
text: About two weeks with the library we evaluated. But it would overlap with the connector work, so we'd need a second engineer.

speaker: Speaker 3
text: We could start hiring the contractor now. I talked to finance, there's budget for one person for three months.

speaker: Me
text: Good. So the proposal is: scheduled exports first, then the Snowflake connector, SAML SSO in parallel with a contractor, and a dashboard design spike in January.

speaker: Speaker 1
text: I can live with that. Exports ship by mid-January.

speaker: Speaker 2
text: Fine for me, as long as dashboards are the headline of Q2 and not postponed again.

speaker: Me
text: Agreed, I'll write that down explicitly. What are the risks we should flag?

speaker: Speaker 3
text: Data volumes. Some exports will hit millions of rows, so we need pagination and a size limit before we promise anything to customers.

speaker: Speaker 1
text: And the Snowflake sandbox account. We still don't have one. Lena, can you ask your contact?

speaker: Speaker 3
text: Sure, I'll ask today.

speaker: Me
text: I'll turn this into a one-pager and share it with the whole team by Friday. Tom, please send me your spike plan before that.

speaker: Speaker 2
text: Will do, Thursday latest.

speaker: Me
text: Great, thanks everyone. That was productive.
